text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
FINANCIEELE DAGBLAD
- Dutch securities trade watchdog STE asks Finance Minister Gerrit Zalm to increase its supervisory powers. (p1)
- Dutch companies invested a record $ 19 billion in buying up foreign firms in 1996, double the 1995 figure, according to accountancy firm KPMG. (p1)
- Philips president Cor Boonstra sharply criticises his predecessor Jan Timmer's strategy. (p1)
- Biotechnology firm Pharming of Leiden is getting ready for a flotation on either the London Stock Exchange, Nasdaq, Easdaq or a combination of two of these exchanges. (p1)
- Printer and copier maker Oce-Van der Grinten books 56 pct higher 1996 net of 169 million guilders; expects further profit growth. (p3)
- Brewer Grolsch and German partner Brau und Brunnen limit distribution and promotion of Grolsch pilsner in Germany. (p3)
- ABN Amro Bank is helping with private placement of shares in the new bourse holding company Amsterdam Exchanges. (p13) DE VOLKSKRANT
- Dutch speed skaters win men's and women's gold at European Championships in Heerenveen. (p1)
- Dutch PTT (KPN) seeks to move parts of its head office to The Hague from Groningen. (p2)
- Some 300 employees of Akzo Nobel's French unit Riom protest in Arnhem against job cuts. (p2)
- German department store chain Tengelmann thinks of withdrawing from Netherlands if its A&P supermarkets fail to gain a 10 percent market share of Dutch market. (p2) DE TELEGRAAF
- Rotterdam police seize chemicals which could be used to make millions of XTC pills. (p1)
- Amsterdam's mayor Schelto Patijn criticises nature conservation association for its interference with the city's expansion plans. (p6)
- KLM loses court case in dispute about control over its U.S. partner Northwest Airlines. (p13) TROUW
- KLM Royal Dutch Airlines is to check wiring of fuel system of its Boeings 747 for risk of explosion following advice received by U.S. FAA. (p1) ALGEMEEN DAGBLAD
- Dutch PTT (KPN) books 21 billion guilder turnover in 1996, eight percent more than in 1995. (p11)
- Philips Electronics to cease marketing of audio-visual consumer electronics products in Japan. (11)
